skill.name: binary-re-static-analysis
skill.description: Analyze binaries without running them using radare2 and Ghidra workflows for function enumeration, cross-reference tracing, decompilation, CFG review, and journaling.
skill.summary: Static reverse-engineering workflow for binary structure, functions, xrefs, and decompilation.
skill.author: 2389-research

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown code fences and inline radare2 command names, not Ruby backtick execution. Real risks remain where the workflow asks an agent to execute sample binaries, install r2ghidra, run shell command substitution over binary-derived names, and create a fixed /tmp Ghidra project. No prompt injection or data exfiltration instructions were found.

remediation.issue: Binary execution appears in a static-analysis workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Move I/O execution to a dynamic-analysis skill, or require an isolated sandbox, no network access, resource limits, and explicit approval.

remediation.issue: The workflow installs r2ghidra during analysis.
remediation.suggestion: Require a preinstalled reviewed toolchain, or pin plugin source, version, and checksum before installation.

remediation.issue: The shell loop expands binary-derived function names without quoting.
remediation.suggestion: Use structured radare2 JSON parsing, or quote and validate every function name before shell expansion.

remediation.issue: The Ghidra project path uses a fixed /tmp directory.
remediation.suggestion: Create a unique directory with mktemp, restrict permissions, and remove it after analysis.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Binary Execution in Static Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The pre-analysis section tells the agent to run the analyzed binary through qemu, Docker, or native execution after approval. This is risky inside a static-analysis skill because unknown binaries may be hostile.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines explicitly require approval and then show qemu, Docker, and native execution of ./binary. The approval language reduces accidental execution risk but does not remove execution risk.

semantic_findings.title: On-Demand Tool Plugin Installation

content.user_title: Analyze Binaries with r2 and Ghidra
content.value_statement: Binary analysis is slow when function maps, xrefs, and decompiler output are scattered. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a staged static-analysis workflow.
actual_capabilities: Guides radare2 light analysis with functions, imports, strings, and cross-references.
Shows how to choose analysis depth based on binary size.
Provides r2ghidra and Ghidra headless steps for targeted decompilation.
Covers CFG, call graph, data structure, network, configuration, and crypto tracing patterns.
Defines a journaling format for facts, hypotheses, questions, and resolved findings.
limitations: It depends on external tools such as radare2, r2ghidra, Ghidra, jq, qemu, and Docker.
It can suggest executing binaries for I/O comparison, which requires approval and sandboxing.
It does not include the referenced Ghidra ExportDecompilation.java script.
It provides analysis workflows, not automated malware containment or legal authorization.

use_cases.title: Map an unknown binary
use_cases.description: Enumerate functions, imports, strings, and xrefs before deeper reverse engineering.

use_cases.title: Trace risky behavior
use_cases.description: Follow network, file, and crypto call chains from imports to caller functions.

use_cases.title: Document firmware findings
use_cases.description: Record facts, hypotheses, and open questions after static analysis of embedded binaries.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Light Pass
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for a new sample
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a light static-analysis pass for this binary. Identify architecture assumptions, function enumeration, imports, strings, and first xrefs to inspect.

prompt_templates.title: Trace a String or Import
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow for a suspicious artifact
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me trace this string or import through the binary. Show which functions reference it and what caller chain to inspect next.

prompt_templates.title: Decompile a Target Function
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for focused reverse engineering
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide a targeted decompilation of this function. Compare decompiler output with disassembly, xrefs, local variables, and control flow.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Evidence Journal
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn these static-analysis notes into facts, hypotheses, confidence levels, unresolved questions, and recommended dynamic checks.

output_examples.input: I have a stripped ARM binary and need a first static pass.
output_examples.output: The skill would propose a light radare2 workflow, list the first artifacts to collect, and defer execution until approval.

output_examples.input: Which function uses this API endpoint string?
output_examples.output: The skill would map the string to an address, inspect xrefs, identify containing functions, and summarize likely data flow.

output_examples.input: I need to record findings after decompiling a function.
output_examples.output: The skill would separate observed facts from hypotheses, cite analysis sources, update confidence, and list open questions.

best_practices: Confirm authorization and isolate samples before using binary analysis tools.
Start with light analysis, then deepen only the functions that matter.
Record facts, source commands, confidence, and unresolved questions.
anti_patterns: Running unknown binaries natively without explicit approval and sandboxing.
Using full deep analysis on large binaries before scoping the target.
Treating decompiler output as ground truth without checking disassembly and xrefs.

faq.question: Does this skill execute binaries by default?
faq.answer: No. Its main workflow is static analysis, but one pre-analysis section suggests approved I/O comparison.

faq.question: Which tools does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects radare2 for core analysis and optionally r2ghidra, Ghidra headless, jq, qemu, and Docker.

faq.question: Can it analyze stripped binaries?
faq.answer: Yes. It focuses on imports, strings, xrefs, function discovery, and targeted decompilation when symbols are absent.

faq.question: Is this only for malware analysis?
faq.answer: No. It also supports firmware review, compatibility debugging, vulnerability research, and unknown binary triage.

faq.question: Does it replace dynamic analysis?
faq.answer: No. It builds hypotheses and recommends dynamic verification when static evidence is incomplete.

faq.question: Can it produce final reverse-engineering reports?
faq.answer: It provides journaling structure and evidence organization, but final conclusions still need analyst review.
